review_method: Actual visual inspection of generated contact sheets at +0.2, +1.0 and +2.0 seconds; green tracker reference and pink predicted first eight fixed point IDs
fixed_cup: One-third displacement shrinks the large arc substantially, but final points curve rightward away from the actual cup. Step-equals-frame remains too high at the end.
fixed_bottle: One-third displacement shrinks the large arc and approaches the bottle better, but rightward displacement and timing differ. Step-equals-frame remains substantially too high/right.
oracle_cup: Smaller oracle and cross-scene scales keep the forecast near the actual cup longer, but residual trajectory direction and endpoint errors remain; these scales used future data.
CASE_AUGE_cup_pilot: Actual recalibration reduces the arc visibly versus baseline. It still overshoots. One-third correction brings middle positions closer while the final arc remains off the object.
CASE_NOK_cup_pilot: The raw forecast changes from a broad rightward arc to a more direct upward lift. One-third correction stays much closer to the actual moving cup in the reviewed frames.
CASE_H1_cup_pilot: The complete actual 8x32 output makes a large placing arc toward the right prematurely; t0-only conditioning does not resolve mismatch during the observed lift phase.
decision: Expand both CASE-AUGE and CASE-NOK to all fixed 24 IDs in both scenes. Both visual pilot effects are substantive. Full runs are in progress sequentially.
limitations: First-eight-point visual inspection does not establish coherence of all 24 predictions.
Only sampled contact-sheet frames reviewed so far; decode/review the complete movies before final claims.
Metrics are secondary, and future-fitted oracle scales are diagnostics.
